What degraded

  • Shipped under the bar
    Shipped at the round cap with a panel median of 7.09, 0.91 under the 8.0 top rung. The craft floor stood down with the art median at 6.5 under 8.5.
  • Frames 6 to 8 leave the motif
    Frames 6, 7 and 8 leave the return plate's iron and brass, and every round 3 judge named it: 6 reads as grey kit clay, 7 as a ruler on a rail, 8 as a safe dial on grey paper.
  • Frames 5 and 3 sit in the mid tones
    Frame 5's tanks read as pucks on a mid-tone floor, and frame 3 keeps a brown haze band behind the hook because print_ban requires a frame calling TXT.sky to show it.
  • One page skeleton
    The page skeleton the storyboard planned to alternate was not built. Eight frames are type over art and one is type as the object.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it 233 data centers never returned the water survey, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

The water board asked by mail. Now ERCOT asks before the power flows.

Records the Texas Tribune obtained for 2020 through 2025 count 334 data center facilities. 233 never submitted a requested water use survey. The Tribune reports a fine of up to $500 for skipping it. The board says it has no authority of its own to prosecute.

Does ERCOT's request reach those 233? Its list is drawn differently. The survey goes only to operating data centers. The request reaches proposed ones of 25 to under 75 MW classed as Substantiated and Batch Zero facilities or additions not yet energized.

ERCOT's September 14th notice puts the water board's questions in Section C. A complete response carries a notarized attestation. A failure to respond is reported to the PUC and the Office of the Governor.

Will the report ERCOT expects to publish by December 10th say how many responded?

#ERCOT #TWDB #BatchZero

The machine changed itself

  • Machine queue, six new items and two repeats raised
    Weekly machine pass not due (last ran October 24th). Six items queued: plate and tank models built in the chassis, the kit substation reading as grey clay, print_ban's sky rule forcing haze on a downward view, the fact-checker never writing claim document titles, gate_status reading out/ while receipts land in runs/, and the article browser test's Playwright import. Two repeats raised: relief height noise under a low key, and a relief plate reading as a tray.

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

Shipped at the round cap. The panel median was 7.09 after three rounds, 0.91 under the 8.0 top rung, and no judge found a hard fail. The art median held at 6.5 and the craft floor stood down at the cap. The record. 44 due items were re-verified and 23 crawl boundaries re-measured, and every boundary held. tx-2026-0171 gained two claims from the Tribune's October 14th report. tx-2026-0231, UT Austin's $643,719 AI movement model award, was admitted on the university's own news item. The Attorney General's October 23rd suit against OpenAI was not admitted, because texasattorneygeneral.gov refuses this project in robots.txt and the petition was unreachable. 35 items carry a dated unconfirmed line, most behind newsroom or county robots refusals. The deck. The water board's mailed survey (334 facilities in the Tribune's records, 233 never returned it, up to $500, no authority to prosecute) set against ERCOT's September 14th notice, which carries the board's Section C questions to proposed and not yet energized data centers. It is drawn as one cast iron return plate in lastLight. c5 was re-fetched from ERCOT's page so frame 7's "Substantiated" carries a verbatim quote. What the judges still name. Frames 6 to 8 leave the plate's iron and brass: a grey kit substation, a copper bar that reads as a ruler, a notarized sheet whose seal reads as a safe dial. Frame 5's tanks read as pucks. Frame 3 keeps a haze band behind the hook. The deck names no county and gives no action, and the county and district attorneys in c33 were the lever it left out. Did the run wait on a human. The reading was taken before the merge, after the last commit. prompt_audit measured 1,718 tool calls and exited 1. 95 calls waited on a permission decision, 67 Bash, 21 Agent, 5 SubagentHandback and 2 SendMessage, from 1.0 to 28.9 seconds each and 460.8 seconds in all. The longest was an Agent spawn at 28.9 seconds. Nothing waited minutes or hours. No-stall hook: armed at 2026-10-25T05:07:20Z. At session start it judged the session unattended (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0), and the host's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED was 0. It refused nothing. Earlier in the run several calls came back with no safety classifier verdict. They were retried, and you were sent a notification that the run might stall. It did not.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
